messages:
alex: Heads-up — I sketched a small panel called Prefetch Creditline Explorer. Compact view: per-route prefetch vs hotpath token credits + per-model unit cost. Posting a proto API I hacked together.

alex: GET /api/v1/costs/prefetch-explorer?route=checkout-web&window=24h

alex: ```json
{
  "route": "checkout-web",
  "window_hours": 24,
  "prefetch_credits": 3421,
  "hotpath_tokens": 128312,
  "credit_allocation": [
    {"tenant": "acct-123", "prefetch_credit": 120},
    {"tenant": "acct-456", "prefetch_credit": 50}
  ],
  "notes": "credits are amortized, sampled at 1%"
}
```

maria: Nice. Quick q — how does this attribute credits for multi-model chains? Do we give the prefetch credit to the first model only or split across the chain? :thinking:

jamal: Prefer per-token lineage. If model A prefetches and k-v is used by B, both should get accounted where appropriate. That means backend needs to join traces / token lineage.

sophie: Joining traces at full-cardinality is heavy and will blow up telemetry. We should approximate: routing hints + model tags to split credits, fallback to sampled lineage.

kevin: Agreed on sampling. Proposal: 1% global sample, full capture for top-10 tenants by spend, and synthetic amplification in the UI to show estimated totals.

alex: Rollout idea: feature-flag, canary to 5% orgs, then 25%. UI shows a badge: "estimated" when sample-based, "exact" when full attribution available.

maria: Also need to think about quotas — if prefetch credit is material we should surface it to per-route quota controls (slider in Console). Otherwise product teams will be surprised.

jamal: We can expose a new metric `prefetch_cost_rate` that quota service can consume. That keeps coupling loose. It's computed in cost service from the same windows.

sophie: API debate: compute `prefetch_cost_rate` inside the cost service (single source of truth) or compute it in proxy by combining token telemetry + routing logs? I vote cost service.

alex: Cost service for truth, yes. Frontend can compute small client-side diffs for interactivity (what-if sliders) but should never be source of truth for billing.

costbot: costbot: Note: backend data freshness ~1h, sample_rate=1%, estimation_error=~±5%. Metric `prefetch_cost_rate` will be tagged with `estimation:sampled` when applicable. :eyes: :chart_with_upwards_trend:

kevin: UX suggestion: add a "what-if" slider to the panel to show cost delta if prefetch disabled for route or throttled by X%. Helpful for PMs.

alex: Good. I'll include that in the RFC and mockups. Also need a perf estimate for the join step; if it's too expensive we'll do a hybrid. @sophie can you run a telemetry volume & cost sim?

sophie: On it — will run numbers (1% vs 0.1% sampling and full trace scenarios) and post by EOD. :thumbsup:

maria: If sampling plan looks risky, we should add a fallback: show a 7-day moving average and surface confidence intervals in the UI.

alex: Agreed. Thanks all — I'll draft an RFC with endpoints, sampling plan, rollout gates, and a small mock. Leaving notes for engineers: backend API must return `estimation_type` and `sample_rate` to make UI clear.

kevin: One more ask — add a tiny export button (CSV) so ops can run quick audits.

alex: Will do. RFC by tomorrow morning.

jamal: +1 — prefer server-side attribution when feasible, but we have clear fallbacks.

sophie: Posted initial telemetry numbers in #eng-infra — linking after I clean them up.

alex: Awesome, thanks.
